topics.title: Chapter overview

Its smaller contract lets you trace allocation, copying, commit, and cleanup. topics.title: 3.1 Understanding Contiguous Memory Layout
topics.summary: Contiguous storage places elements next to one another in the array’s element order. An index maps to an element offset, supporting constant-time random access under the ordinary address-arithmetic model.

paragraphs: For an array base and valid index i, the conceptual address offset is i * sizeof(T) bytes within the appropriate object representation. C++ pointer arithmetic performs element stepping directly, so code uses data[i] or data + i rather than manually inventing byte offsets for typed access.

A dynamic owner must preserve the invariant size <= capacity and ensure the active sequence’s indices are below size. Capacity describes available storage, while size describes the logical sequence. In this integer-only teaching implementation, the allocated array actually constructs all capacity integers; that differs from a fully generic vector managing raw capacity without live elements in every slot.

For a contiguous sequence of T objects, moving from one element to the next advances by sizeof(T) bytes in the object representation. C++ pointer arithmetic already accounts for that scale: data + i identifies the ith element, not the byte at offset i. Multiplying by sizeof(T) again in a typed pointer expression is a common low-level mistake.

The remaining capacity is not permission to access positions three through seven with operator[] on a standard vector. Representation details do not override the public contract.

topics.title: 3.1.2 Exploiting Cache Locality
topics.summary: Sequential traversal often benefits from spatial locality because nearby values can be fetched together through the memory hierarchy. A linked traversal may require discovering each next address before proceeding. These are architectural tendencies, not universal timing guarantees.

blocks.text: Contiguity helps a sequential scan because nearby logical elements occupy nearby storage. A processor commonly transfers and caches memory in blocks, so consuming adjacent entries can reuse data brought in for neighboring entries. The exact cache-line size, prefetch behavior, and latency depend on the machine; the layout argument does not require declaring one particular device geometry universal.

blocks.text: Consider summing the readings in order versus following an index chain that jumps among them. Both can perform one addition per reading, but the chain introduces a dependency: the next location is not known until the previous location is read. Contiguous iteration often gives the implementation more opportunity to fetch ahead. Chapter 20 measures a related traversal difference while preserving an identical numerical result.

blocks.text: Contiguity is not a guarantee that every object contains its payload inline. A vector of strings stores string objects contiguously, while some character data may live in separate allocations. A vector of owning pointers stores pointers contiguously, not necessarily the pointed-to nodes. Ask which bytes the hot loop actually touches before concluding that choosing vector removed all indirection.

blocks.text: Layout also affects mutation cost. Inserting at the beginning of a contiguous sequence can require moving later values so that positions remain packed. A node-based structure avoids that particular shift when the insertion location is already known, but may pay for allocation and traversal. Comparing only the final pointer update with a full vector insertion omits the work needed to locate the node.

Comparing only the final pointer update with a full vector insertion omits the work needed to locate the node.

blocks.text: Use workload descriptions rather than container slogans. “Append batches, scan all samples, rarely insert in the middle” is a stronger basis for choosing a vector than “vectors are fast.” If a caller needs stable addresses across growth, the representation or interface may need to change. Reserving a justified capacity can postpone relocation, but it does not create an unlimited address-stability guarantee.

blocks.text: Finally, measure the same operation on the same data. An array loop that sums integers cannot fairly be compared with a linked structure that parses strings during traversal. Locality is one variable in an experiment, not an excuse to change the problem being solved.

Write the lifetime ledger for old elements, successfully constructed replacement elements, and unconstructed replacement storage. blocks.text: Review reasoning. Why can an index equal to capacity be invalid even when memory was allocated? Because the public sequence is bounded by size. Why does reserve not insert values? It changes storage availability, not membership. Why is integer-by-value useful for aliased append? It captures the value before growth. Why is temporary peak memory larger than the final buffer? The old and replacement allocations coexist until commit. Why not advertise this as a drop-in vector? It intentionally omits general element lifetime, allocator, copy, and iterator semantics.
